title: Completeness of the SS-ID Algorithm as a Nonidentification Procedure under Confounded Selection
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field); not salvageable within scope, with unrepaired D0.5 findings preserved in the review receipts.
proof_attempt_summary: The run classified four three-node terminal masks, built explicit counterexamples and obstruction results, and derived exact finite semialgebraic criteria for fixed-specification nonidentification and outside-model amalgamation. It did not extend those results to the forty-two four-node terminal fibers or arbitrary LS-ADMMGs, so the field-level completeness program collapsed to an incremental finite decision formulation. D0.5 also stopped before repairing the source-trace proof gap, the perfect-instrument prior-art positioning, and the unsupported claim that the m-state bound is sharp.
tldr: Literal printed SS-ID is not complete as a nonidentification procedure. In the exact three-node audit, terminal masks are \(3,5,6,7\): masks \(3,6,7\) have positive same-full-law separating SCM pairs, while mask \(5\) is uniformly identified by \(\Phi_B(P)(b)=P(Y=b\mid S=(1,1))\). For a nonempty outside set, closure-to-full-model amalgamation is decided exactly by finite graph- and label-compatible multilinear programs. In each unrestricted separate program, with \(m=|\operatorname{Adm}(B)|\), every new outside-only root needs at most \(m\) states, and this is the sharp guaranteed bound supplied by the one-model simplex argument. In the optional paired common-mechanism program, a matched new root whose single law must preserve both models needs at most \(2m-1\) states; this is a valid general bound, not a claimed sharp global lower bound. More generally, for \(k\) laidback-outcome cells, point nonidentification at a fixed positive law is equivalent to feasibility of a finite paired semialgebraic catalogue with at most \(m+k-1\) states per consolidated root; point identification is infeasibility, and failure of uniform identification is the analogous feasibility problem with a common positive law variable. These decision criteria do not make every terminal input nonidentified.
gap: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser leave Algorithm 2 line 9 outside their nonidentification theorem. The former proposed universal printed/worked trace equality is false because serious-child deletion can alter the line-6 district.
fill: Use only the literal source trace, reclassify the 72 bounded graphs, prove simultaneous-context separation and label-preserving extension for every positive source-terminal law, or turn the first point-identified law into a uniform rule on a nontrivial varying-law class.
